name: Mathematics
blurb: Arithmetic, algebra, geometry, and data rebuilt from the ground up, with checkpoint exams that gate each group of topics.

nodes.title: Start Here
nodes.description: Take a short diagnostic across arithmetic, algebra, geometry, and data. Clear this node to open the first group of topics in every branch.
nodes.tip: Log each miss by topic; your weakest three topics become the first subskills you study.

nodes.title: Operations & Number Sense
nodes.description: Integer rules, order of operations, divisibility, primes, and the number properties UPCAT leans on.
nodes.tip: Drill 20 order-of-operations items daily; write each step instead of computing in your head.

nodes.title: Fractions, Decimals & Percents
nodes.description: Convert fluently between forms and handle percent change, discounts, and fractional parts.
nodes.tip: Memorize the fraction–percent table (1/8 = 12.5%, 1/6 ≈ 16.7%) so you can skip long division.

nodes.title: Ratios & Proportions
nodes.description: Part-to-part and part-to-whole ratios, direct and inverse proportion, and scaling.
nodes.tip: When a problem gives a ratio, assign a multiplier x and express every quantity in terms of x.

nodes.title: Algebraic Expressions
nodes.description: Simplify expressions, combine like terms, expand, and translate words into algebra.
nodes.tip: Underline the unknown and write a 'let x =' line before touching the equation.

nodes.title: Linear Equations
nodes.description: Solve one- and two-variable linear equations, interpret slope, and check solutions.
nodes.tip: Whatever you do to one side, do to the other, then substitute your answer back in.

nodes.title: Inequalities & Absolute Value
nodes.description: Solve linear inequalities, compound inequalities, and simple absolute-value equations.
nodes.tip: Flip the inequality sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative number.

nodes.title: Lines, Angles & Triangles
nodes.description: Angle relationships, triangle properties, congruence, and the exterior angle theorem.
nodes.tip: Draw the figure even when one is provided, and mark every given value on it.

nodes.title: Coordinate Geometry
nodes.description: Distance, midpoint, slope, and equations of lines on the Cartesian plane.
nodes.tip: Sketch the points; most coordinate problems become obvious once the segment or triangle is drawn.

nodes.title: Tables, Graphs & Charts
nodes.description: Read tables, bar graphs, line graphs, and pie charts without misreading labels or units.
nodes.tip: Read the axis labels and units before the question; most traps live in 'percent of what?'.

nodes.title: Foundations Exam
nodes.description: Checkpoint covering number operations, fractions, ratios, expressions, linear relationships, inequalities, angles, coordinates, and data displays.
nodes.tip: Score 80% or higher to master this checkpoint and unlock the next group. Review every explanation before retrying.

questions.explanation: Inside the parentheses: 5 − 3 = 2. Square it to get 4, then multiply by 2 to get 8, and finally add 8. The result is 16.
Distribute the 3 to get 6x − 12, then combine like terms: 6x + 5x = 11x. The simplified expression is 11x − 12.
Subtract 5 from both sides to get 2x > 8, then divide by the positive 2. The inequality sign stays the same: x > 4.

questions.prompt: A recipe uses flour and sugar in a 3:2 ratio. If you use 18 cups of flour, how many cups of sugar do you need?
questions.explanation: The ratio 3:2 means sugar = (2/3) × flour. So sugar = (2/3) × 18 = 12 cups.

questions.prompt: The angles of a triangle are 2x, 3x, and 4x. What is the value of x?
questions.explanation: The angles of a triangle sum to 180°, so 2x + 3x + 4x = 9x = 180. Dividing gives x = 20.

nodes.title: Estimation & Mental Math
nodes.description: Approximate before you compute, sanity-check answer choices, and use friendly benchmarks.
nodes.tip: Round first. UPCAT choices are often far enough apart that an estimate eliminates three options.

nodes.title: Rates, Work & Mixture
nodes.description: Speed–distance–time, combined work, and mixture problems solved with clean tables.
nodes.tip: Use the units to decide the operation: 'of the job per hour' means your rates add.

nodes.title: Advanced Word Problems
nodes.description: Translate multi-step age, digit, investment, and geometry word problems into equations.
nodes.tip: Write the final question as a sentence with a blank; it tells you exactly what to solve for.

nodes.title: Polynomials & Factoring
nodes.description: Expand, factor, and simplify polynomials including difference of squares and trinomials.
nodes.tip: Always check for a greatest common factor before trying any other factoring pattern.

nodes.title: Systems of Equations
nodes.description: Solve two-variable systems by substitution and elimination; recognize no-solution cases.
nodes.tip: Elimination is faster when coefficients line up — multiply to create opposites, then add.

nodes.title: Sequences & Series
nodes.description: Arithmetic and geometric sequences, nth terms, and simple series sums.
nodes.tip: List the first four terms before hunting for a formula — the pattern is usually visible.

nodes.title: Circles, Area & Volume
nodes.description: Circle measures plus perimeter, area, surface area, and volume of solids.
nodes.tip: Keep a one-page formula sheet and re-derive it weekly so the formulas actually stick.

nodes.title: Polygons & Quadrilaterals
nodes.description: Interior and exterior angles of polygons, parallelogram properties, and trapezoid area.
nodes.tip: The interior angles of an n-sided polygon sum to (n − 2) × 180°.

nodes.title: Averages & Weighted Mean
nodes.description: Mean, median, mode, range, and weighted averages in mixed data sets.
nodes.tip: For weighted mean, convert each weight into a fraction of the total before multiplying.

nodes.title: Counting & Probability
nodes.description: Permutations, combinations, and single- and multi-event probability.
nodes.tip: Ask whether order matters: order matters → permutation, order does not → combination.

nodes.title: Core Skills Exam
nodes.description: Checkpoint covering estimation, rates, advanced word problems, polynomials, systems, sequences, circles, polygons, averages, and probability.
nodes.tip: Score 80% or higher to master this checkpoint and unlock the advanced group.

questions.explanation: Round each value: 50 × 20 ÷ 10 = 100. The exact answer is close to 100.
This is a difference of squares: a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b). Here a = x and b = 3.

questions.prompt: Solve the system: x + y = 7 and x − y = 1
questions.explanation: Adding the equations eliminates y: 2x = 8, so x = 4. Then 4 + y = 7 gives y = 3.

questions.prompt: What is the next term in the sequence 3, 7, 11, 15, …?
questions.explanation: The sequence increases by 4 each time, so the next term is 15 + 4 = 19.

questions.prompt: A circle has radius 5. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Area of a circle is πr². With r = 5, the area is π × 25 = 25π.

nodes.title: Percent, Interest & Growth
nodes.description: Percent increase and decrease, simple and compound interest, and successive percentage changes.
nodes.tip: A 20% increase followed by a 20% decrease does not return to the original value; multiply the factors.

nodes.title: Number Theory & Sets
nodes.description: LCM, GCF, remainders, prime factorisation, and basic set counting with Venn diagrams.
nodes.tip: Use prime factorisation for LCM and GCF; it makes the relationship between them obvious.

nodes.title: Quadratic Equations
nodes.description: Solve by factoring, completing the square, and the quadratic formula; read parabolas.
nodes.tip: Check the discriminant first; it tells you how many real roots to expect before you solve.

nodes.title: Functions & Graphs
nodes.description: Function notation, domain and range, transformations, and graph interpretation.
nodes.tip: Test one input value to match a graph to an equation — faster than analyzing the whole shape.

nodes.title: Exponents & Radicals
nodes.description: Laws of exponents, scientific notation, simplifying radicals, and rationalising denominators.
nodes.tip: Convert radicals to fractional exponents when you need to combine or simplify them.

nodes.title: Similarity & Right Triangles
nodes.description: Similar figures, Pythagorean triples, and basic right-triangle trigonometry.
nodes.tip: Memorize 3-4-5, 5-12-13, and 8-15-17 so you can skip the Pythagorean theorem on test day.

nodes.title: Transformations & Symmetry
nodes.description: Translations, rotations, reflections, dilations, and symmetry in the coordinate plane.
nodes.tip: Track one vertex through the transformation; the rest of the figure follows the same rule.

nodes.title: Data Interpretation
nodes.description: Compare data sets, compute rates from tables, and spot misleading scales or missing baselines.
nodes.tip: Before answering, identify the denominator behind every percentage in the chart.

nodes.title: Statistics & Spread
nodes.description: Range, quartiles, standard deviation concepts, and how outliers move the mean and median.
nodes.tip: An outlier pulls the mean toward itself but barely moves the median.

nodes.title: Advanced Math Exam
nodes.description: Checkpoint covering percent growth, number theory, quadratics, functions, exponents and radicals, similarity, transformations, data interpretation, and statistics.
nodes.tip: Score 80% or higher to master this checkpoint and unlock the final simulation.

questions.prompt: What are the roots of x² − 5x + 6 = 0?
questions.explanation: Factor the quadratic as (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0. Setting each factor equal to zero gives x = 2 or x = 3.

questions.prompt: A right triangle has legs 6 and 8. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
questions.explanation: Use the Pythagorean theorem: 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100, so the hypotenuse is √100 = 10.

nodes.title: Timed Math Simulation
nodes.description: Full mixed math sets under the official time limit, followed by an error-log review.
nodes.tip: Simulate the real clock, then tag every miss by topic. Retake only your two weakest topics first.
